questions.question: / State whether tautology, contradiction, and contingency are mutually exclusive. Explain shortly
questions.solution_html:
•  Yes, they are mutually exclusive. (1 mark)
  • A tautology is always true, a contradiction is always false
  • and a contingency is sometimes true and sometimes false. (1 mark)
questions.final_answer: and a contingency is sometimes true and sometimes false

questions.question: Compare distributive law in sets with distributive law in arithmetic.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare distributive law in sets with distributive law in arithmetic.
  •  Set theory: 𝐴 ∩ (𝐵 ∪ 𝐶) = (𝐴 ∩ 𝐵) ∪ (𝐴 ∩ 𝐶) (1 mark)
  • Arithmetic: 𝑎 × (𝑏 + 𝑐) = 𝑎×𝑏 + 𝑎×𝑐
  • Comparison: Both show how one operation distributes over another.(1 mark)
questions.final_answer: Comparison: Both show how one operation distributes over another
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
